content.value_statement: Next.js caching can be hard to apply safely across static, cached, and dynamic content. This skill gives Claude, Codex, and Claude Code practical guidance for Cache Components.
actual_capabilities: Explains how to enable Cache Components with cacheComponents in next.config.ts.
Distinguishes static, cached, and dynamic content in App Router pages.
Shows use cache, cacheLife, cacheTag, updateTag, and revalidateTag patterns.
Documents runtime data constraints for cookies, headers, and search parameters.
Provides migration guidance from older Next.js caching options.
Summarizes limitations for Edge runtime, static export, and non-deterministic values.
limitations: It is documentation guidance, not an automated migration tool.
It does not validate a real application against current Next.js behavior.
It does not include tests or executable helper scripts.
It focuses on Next.js 16 Cache Components only.

use_cases.title: Plan Cache Component Adoption
use_cases.description: Map each page section to static, cached, or dynamic rendering before changing application code.

use_cases.title: Review Cache Invalidation Design
use_cases.description: Choose cache tags and invalidation methods for product, post, or dashboard data flows.

use_cases.title: Prepare Migration Notes
use_cases.description: Convert older caching concepts into Cache Components terminology for an upgrade plan.

prompt_templates.title: Classify Page Content
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this Next.js page and classify each section as static, cached, or dynamic. Explain the safest Cache Components approach.

prompt_templates.title: Add Cached Data Loading
prompt_templates.prompt: Help me add use cache and cacheLife to this data-loading component. Keep runtime request data outside the cached function.

prompt_templates.title: Design Tag Invalidation
prompt_templates.prompt: Design cacheTag, updateTag, and revalidateTag usage for these mutation paths. Explain when each invalidation method should run.

prompt_templates.title: Plan a Migration
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a migration plan from older Next.js caching options to Cache Components. Include risks, testing steps, and rollout order.

output_examples.input: A dashboard page mixes navigation, hourly stats, and user notifications.
output_examples.output: The response separates the static shell, cached stats, and dynamic notifications. It recommends Suspense for fresh user-specific data.

output_examples.input: A product update action must show fresh data immediately after saving.
output_examples.output: The response recommends tagging product cache entries and using immediate invalidation after the mutation completes.

output_examples.input: A team needs to replace older caching settings during an upgrade.
output_examples.output: The response maps each old setting to the newer Cache Components pattern and lists validation steps.

best_practices: Classify rendering needs before adding cache directives.
Keep request-specific runtime APIs outside shared cached functions.
Use cache tags that match the data model and mutation paths.
anti_patterns: Do not cache personalized data without a private cache strategy.
Do not rely on random or time-based values inside shared cached output.
Do not use broad invalidation when a precise tag can refresh the affected data.

faq.question: What does this skill help with?
faq.answer: It helps agents reason about Next.js 16 Cache Components, cache lifetimes, tags, invalidation, and migration choices.

faq.question: Does it run commands or modify files?
faq.answer: No. The skill is a Markdown guide with examples. It does not include executable scripts.

faq.question: Can it migrate an application automatically?
faq.answer: No. It can guide a migration plan, but implementation still requires project-specific code changes and tests.

faq.question: When should I use use cache?
faq.answer: Use it when data can be reused safely across requests and does not depend directly on request-only APIs.

faq.question: How does it handle personalized data?
faq.answer: It explains the runtime data constraint and points to private caching when refactoring is not practical.

faq.question: Which tools can use this skill?
faq.answer: The report lists support for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.
